annotations.title: Defrauded.
annotations.text: In that (saith S. Augustine) <mn>[1]</mn> he withdrew any part of that vvhich he promised, he vvas guilty at once, both of sacrilege, <mn>[2]</mn>and of fraude. of sacrilege, because he robbed God of that vvhich vvas his by promes: of fraude, in that he vvithheld of the vvhole gift, a peece. Let novv the Heretikes come, and say it vvas for lying or hypocrisie onely that this facte vvas condemned: because they be loth to haue sacrilege counted any such sinne, vvho haue taught men not onely to take avvay from God some peece of that or al that them selues gaue, but plainly to spoile & apply to them selues al that other men gaue.

notes.text: Aug. ser. 9. in append. de diuersis tom. 10.

annotations.title: Peter said.
annotations.text: S. Peter (as you see here) vvithout mans relation knevv this fraude and the cogitations of Ananias, and as head of the College and of the vvhole Church against vvhich this robbery vvas committed, executed this heauy sentence of Excommunication [1] both against him, and his vvife consenting to the Sacrilege. for it vvas excommunication by S. Augustines iudgement, (li. 3 cont. ep. Parm. c. 1 to. 7) and had this corporal miraculous death ioyned vvithal, as the Excommunication that S. Paul [2] gaue out against the incestuous and others, had the corporal vexation of Satan incident vnto it.

annotations.title: In thy povver.
annotations.text: [1] If it displeased God (saith S. Augustine) to vvithdravv of the money vvhich they had vovved to God, hovv is he angry vvhen chastitie is vovved and is not performed? for to such may be said that vvhich S. Peter said of the money: Thy virginitie remaining did it not remaine to thee, and before thou didst vovv, vvas it not in thine ovvne povver? for, vvhosoeuer haue vovved such things and haue not paied them, let them not thinke to be condemned to corporal deaths, but to euerlasting fire. August. Ser. 10. de diuersis. And S. Gregorie [2] to the same purpose vvriteth thus, Ananias had vovved money to God, vvhich aftervvard ouercome vvith diuelish persuasion he vvithdrevv: but vvith vvhat death he vvas punished, thou knovvest. If then he vvere vvorthy of that death, vvho tooke avvay the money that he had giuen to God, consider vvhat great peril in Gods iudgement thou shalt be vvorthy of, vvhich hast vvithdravven, not money, but thy self from almighty God, to vvhom thou hadst vovved thy self vnder the habite or vveede of a Monke.

notes.text: Vovv of Chastitie, & the breache thereof.

annotations.title: Not to men, but.
annotations.text: To take from the Church or from the Gouernours thereof, things dedicated to their vse and the seruice of God, or to lie vnto Gods Ministers, is so iudged of before God, as if the lie vvere made, and the fraude done to the Holy Ghost him self, vvho is the Churches President and Protector.

annotations.title: His shadovv.
annotations.text: ◦ Specially they sought to Peter the cheefe of al, vvho not onely by touching, as the other, but by his very shadovv cured al diseases. vvhere vpon S. Augustine saith, If then the shadovv of his body could helpe, hovv much more novv the fulnes of povver? And if then a certaine litle vvind of him passing by did profite them that humbly asked, hovv much more the grace of him novv being permanent & remaining? Ser. 29. de Sanctis, speaking of the miracles done by the Saincts novv reigning in heauen.
